Baptists N.C. Baptists will gather for the 2026 annual meeting Nov. 16-17 in Greensboro. N.C. Baptists will once again gather under the theme of “On Mission Together” for the 2026 Baptist State Convention of North Carolina annual meeting, which is scheduled for Nov. 16-17 at the Joseph S. Koury Convention Center in Greensboro. This year marks the sixth consecutive year that “On Mission Together” has served as the meeting’s theme, and state convention leaders say the phrase has come to describe the shared identity and mission of N.C. Baptists. “‘On Mission Together’ might have been just a slogan when we started, but it really is who we are as N.C. Baptists,” said Todd Unzicker, N.C. Baptist executive director-treasurer (EDT). “We see that in so many ways, and we look forward to celebrating how God is working across our state at this year’s annual meeting.” The supporting verse for this year’s meeting is Matthew 5:16, which says, “In the same way, let your light shine before others, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father who is in heaven” (ESV). Highlights of this year’s meeting include a Sending Celebration featuring missionaries commissioned by N.C. Baptist churches, a special recognition of N.C. Baptist church plants and sending churches, and the launch of new video-based ministry and discipleship resources developed by N.C. Baptist staff. Trevin Wax, an author, editor and Bible teacher known for helping Christians engage culture with biblical wisdom and theological depth, will deliver this year’s convention sermon. A former missionary to Romania, Wax has written numerous books and regularly contributes to both Christian and mainstream publications. He serves as vice president of resources and marketing with the North American Mission Board and is a visiting professor at Cedarville University. Unzicker will also deliver his annual EDT report to messengers, and state convention President J. Allen Murray, pastor of Mount Pisgah Baptist Church in Supply, will share the annual president’s address. The meeting will also include times of worship, ministry reports, exhibits, breakout sessions, special events and more. The meeting will be preceded by the annual N.C. Baptist Pastors’ Conference on Nov. 15-16. Registration for messengers and guests will open Sept. 15. Attendees may also reserve a room online for the convention center hotel at a special discounted rate of $129 per room, per night, through Oct. 14. After Oct. 14, those wishing to stay on site must make their reservations directly with the convention hotel, which is the Sheraton Four Seasons. Complete information about this year’s annual meeting, including the event schedule, registration details, hotel information and more is available at www.ncannualmeeting.org . More information will be added leading up to the meeting as it becomes available. Information about this year’s N.C. Baptist Pastors’ Conference is available at www.ncpastorsconference.org . Related
